label: Acid curd
comment: Set by acid: the milk soured until it curdles. Made industrially from skimmed milk, fermented on its own; traditionally, soured milk set and drained.

about.text: Curd is obtained by coagulating milk in a sequential process called curdling. It can be a final dairy product or the first stage in cheesemaking. The coagulation can be caused by adding rennet, a culture, or any edible acidic substance such as lemon juice or vinegar, and then allowing it to coagulate. The increased acidity causes the milk proteins (casein) to tangle into solid masses, or curds. Milk that has been left to sour will also automatically produce curds, and sour milk cheeses are produced this way.
